root_cause.text: In `cpuidle_select()` the cpuidle core always delegated state selection to the governor even when the driver exposed only one idle state, allowing the ladder governor to misinterpret a lone polling state as requiring state index 1 and pass an out-of-bounds/NULL idle-state callback into `cpuidle_enter_state()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early bail-out in `cpuidle_select()` for `drv->state_count <= 1` that returns state 0 directly and sets `*stop_tick = false`, and the CVE text says the ladder governor “may incorrectly treat state 1 as the first usable state and pass an out-of-bounds index,” leading to a “NULL enter callback being invoked” and crash.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip governor selection and keep the tick running when only one or no idle states are available.
intent_record.what: In cpuidle_select(), a new early-return block was added before the governor callback: if drv->state_count is less than or equal to 1, it sets *stop_tick to false and returns state index 0. A comment explaining this behavior was also inserted.
intent_record.how: When a CPU idle driver exposes zero or one idle state, the governor is no longer consulted. Instead, the code deterministically selects the first idle state and keeps the scheduler tick running, avoiding meaningless governor selection and any attempt to stop the tick in this degenerate case.

grouping_result.intent: Skip governor selection and keep the tick running when only one or no idle states are available.

relevance_review.reason: The change matches the root cause directly: it avoids governor-based state selection when only one or no idle states exist, preventing the ladder governor from misinterpreting a lone polling state and selecting an invalid idle-state index.

candidates.rationale: This statement always delegates idle-state selection to the governor, even when the driver has only one or no idle states. That allows the governor to choose an invalid state index, leading to an out-of-bounds or NULL callback passed into cpuidle_enter_state().

vuln_statements.explanation: This line always hands state selection to the governor, even when the cpuidle driver exposes only one or no idle states. In that case the ladder governor can mis-handle the lone polling state and return an invalid state index, which then leads to an out-of-bounds or NULL idle-state callback being passed into cpuidle_enter_state().
